answer: A stake-weighted reputation graph can limit sybil attacks: agents lock scarce tokens, and their attestations count only after independent peers verify useful work over repeated rounds. The trellis caps how much influence linked identities gain, while new accounts start with little weight. A nebula of fake agents cannot quickly earn trust; the attacker must lock capital in each and risk losing it for false claims. Reputation grows at a glacier’s pace, imposing a real time and funding cost.
